title: Concept · Traffic light · Inference
description: How fast the served model is running, what each request holds and how close it is to a limit. Opens on the last 15 minutes at one-second detail and refreshes every five seconds.

panels.description: The model, recipe, runtime and host on each successful scrape younger than ten seconds.
The engine's own health flag, on a scrape younger than ten seconds. Broken means a fault has stopped it serving; /health gives the first cause.
Requests in prefill or decode, out of the four streams the engine runs at once, and requests queued until a stream is free.
Tokens per second across all streams, finished and in flight, over the last ten seconds.
Decode speed of one reply, averaged over finished requests in the last five minutes.
The largest running request's share of its context window. Idle when nothing is running.
Share of prompt tokens found cached, over finished requests in the last 15 minutes.
Share of the shared context pool held by streams and kept prompts. It is allocated at startup, so a full pool evicts kept prompts rather than costing memory.

panels.title: Tokens held by each running request
panels.description: Tokens in each running request's cache. Each track is usually one conversation growing turn by turn, and a gap is a request between turns. All one colour because the metrics carry no request id, so a colour could not follow a request. Hover for exact values. A recipe that reports no window size shows nothing here.

targets.expr: (tensorfold:kv_cache_usage_ratio{job="spark-inference",platform="spark",model=~"$model",recipe=~"$recipe",instance=~"$serving_host"} * on (instance, recipe) group_left tensorfold_health:context_length{job="spark-inference",platform="spark",model=~"$model",recipe=~"$recipe",instance=~"$serving_host"}) and on(job,instance,model,recipe,runtime) (up{job="spark-inference",platform="spark",model=~"$model",recipe=~"$recipe",instance=~"$serving_host"} == 1 and (time() - timestamp(up{job="spark-inference",platform="spark",model=~"$model",recipe=~"$recipe",instance=~"$serving_host"}) < 10))

panels.title: Output · tok/s
panels.description: Tokens written across all streams, as they are written. Includes idle time. Amber is every stream busy and red is requests waiting.

panels.title: Decode per reply · tok/s
panels.description: Tokens per second of each reply's own decode time, over finished requests. Concurrent replies share the GPU, so this falls as more run, which the bands show.

panels.title: Prefill · new tok/s
panels.description: Prompt tokens not found in cache, per second of prefill time, over finished requests. Cached tokens take no prefill.

panels.title: Time to first token
panels.description: Server arrival to first generated token. Counts of finished requests in each latency bucket, one column per step of at least a minute. Buckets above ten seconds are wide: 30, 60, 120 and 300 s.

panels.title: Request latency
panels.description: Server arrival to reply completion. Counts of finished requests in each latency bucket, one column per step of at least a minute. Buckets above ten seconds are wide: 30, 60, 120 and 300 s.

panels.title: Mean latency
panels.description: Mean over finished requests, recorded at completion. First token ends at the first generated token, not necessarily the first text a client sees.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: The most requests running and waiting in each step, against the streams the engine runs at once.

panels.title: Completed requests
panels.description: Requests finished in each step of at least a minute. The step grows with the range, so compare heights within one view.

panels.title: Prompt tokens read · tok/s
panels.description: Prompt tokens of finished requests, booked at completion. Only the new ones take prefill time. A recipe that reports no cache shows one total.

panels.title: Pool used
panels.description: Share of the shared pool held by streams and kept prompts, not host memory.

panels.title: Decode round time
panels.description: Milliseconds of decode per round, averaged over finished requests. It rises as more replies run at once, and unlike tokens per second it does not move with draft acceptance.

panels.title: Speculative acceptance
panels.description: Accepted divided by drafted tokens across finished requests.

options.content: Decode, prefill and cache figures average finished requests, so they lag a running reply. Client-visible latency, queue-wait duration and error counts are not measured. [Monitoring notes](https://github.com/kelchm/home-lab/blob/main/sparks/monitoring/README.md).
